summary: Johann III Bernoulli worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Neuchâtel and the University of Basel under Daniel Bernoulli, earning a philosophy doctorate (~1757-1758). He was a member of the Prussian, Russian, and Danzig scientific academies.
Johann Jakob Engel was a philosopher who studied at the University of Rostock (~1757-1762) and the University of Leipzig (~1762-1764). He also taught Wilhelm von Humboldt.

Johann Joachim Winckelmann was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1736), the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1738-1740), and the University of Jena (1741-1742).
Johann Michael Ackner studied under Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren and Christian Gottlob Heyne around 1805 to 1807.

Johann Tobias Beck worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tübingen (~1822-1826), he held posts at the University of Basel (~1836-1843) and the University of Tübingen (~1843-1878).

Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen and the University of Tübingen. He held professorships at the Imperial University of Dorpat/Tartu (1803), the University of Würzburg (1817), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1818).

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Leiden University and under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University. She taught at Groningen and Cambridge, and directed the Institute of South Asian Archaeology at Amsterdam (1958-1983).

Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Saarland University under Ernst Zinn and completed her PhD and habilitation under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she was an Assistentin (1973-1977).

Johannes Beltz works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned doctorates by 1999 at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under supervisors Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst.

Johannes Bronkhorst was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Rajasthan, Pune University under Shivram Dattatray Joshi, and Leiden University. He served as professor at the University of Lausanne from 1987 to 2011.

Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1934-1939) and held academic posts at SOAS University of London (~1957-1979) and as professor at Leiden University (1978-1986).

Johannes Hertel was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig (1892-1897). He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898-1919) and held the chair for Indian Philology at the University of Leipzig from 1919 to 1937.

Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber (1868-1872) and earned a doctorate at the University of Halle (~1869-1873). From 1872 onward, he worked at the Prussian State Library, serving as custodian (1880) and librarian (1889).

Johannes Nobel specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Greifswald and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. After posts at the Prussian State Library and Berlin, he held the Indology chair at the University of Marburg from 1928 to 1955.

Johannes Rahder worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology. He earned a doctorate at Utrecht University (~1920-1926), later serving as professor at Utrecht (1930-1931), Leiden (1931-1946), and Yale University (1947-1965).

Johannes Schmidt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn, under August Schleicher at Jena, and under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1868), University of Graz (1873-1876), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1876).

Johannes Schneider works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Marburg, he held posts at Freie Universität Berlin, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich, becoming an extraordinary professor of Indology in 2014.

Johannes Schubert worked in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at the University of Leipzig under teachers including Conrady, Francke, and Franke. He served at the Leipzig University Library (~1927-1954) and held a Tibetology chair at Leipzig University (1960-1962).

John A. Ardussi works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He was supervised by Turrell V. Wylie for his MA, completed a PhD at Australian National University (attested 1977), and served as a research team member at CNRS.
John A. Brinkman is a scholar of history and archaeology. He held a post at the University of Chicago (~1964) and served as a professor at the University of Oxford (attested 1999).
